place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 242, 247, 250, 242 Birch Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; gable end with a brick-corbelled parapet facing the street, twin arched entries under a small flat hood, a glazed sunporch, and a steel water tower rising behind; a wood privacy fence along the side lot.

facade.notes: the same plan: a side-gabled brick duplex with paired arched doors, an enclosed sunroom on the end; a wooden privacy fence screening the service yard behind; the base water tower rising beyond

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
1920s-30s military housing used Colonial Revival brick for dignity and economy (Quartermaster standard plans)
service yards screened behind institutional housing
